tasks.short: Check applicants against the vacancy and send the matches to the recruiter.

today.trigger: A new application lands in Recruitee, or a recruiter asks for a sift before interviews.
steps: Open the vacancy text on SharePoint and the pipeline in Recruitee.
Read each CV and application, often a mix of Dutch and rough translations.
Check hard requirements: driving licence, VCA, forklift or food-safety certificate, site, shift, and right to work.
Mark the stage, type a note, and refer matches to the recruiter or hiring manager.
Chase missing scans and answer the manager's follow-up questions.
drudgery: Reading the same order-picker and driver CVs again
Retyping a pass or fail note into Recruitee
Chasing a missing forklift or VCA scan
Repeating the sift for Tilburg and Venlo after the Rotterdam day has started
today.time_sinks: Peak season stacks warehouse applications overnight, and night-shift managers wait until the office opens before anyone is referred.

lenses.faster: The first read of each CV against the written knockouts disappears, and clear misses arrive already marked with the failed item. The admin still spends a few minutes on every unclear file and on every name they refer. About 45% of the task time goes.
lenses.autonomous: A new Recruitee application starts a checklist against that vacancy's knockout list. The checklist does not move anyone forward. The admin refers the people they accept.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift hiring managers at Tilburg and Venlo get a same-morning requirement check on applications that came in overnight, a group that now waits for Rotterdam office hours. Demand would grow if this were cheap, because seasonal peaks would ask for the same check on every wave, not only the hard-to-fill driver roles.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss the tenth similar CV. The work they keep is the conversation with the manager about who can actually start on that shift.
lenses.options: Three lists — certificates only, certificates or equivalent experience, and internal or flex-to-perm staff first — change who is interviewed, and that changes time to hire and who is still productive at day 90.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts to unclear files and to vacancies whose requirements are incomplete or unlawful. They can send a vacancy back until the licence class, site, and certificates are explicit. The job becomes more expert on what each CAO role actually requires, and less of a CV reading queue.
reach: Recruiter: chasing incomplete applications and tidying pipeline stages before interview, after they learn which certificates are hard knockouts per site.
Learning and Development Specialist: checking that a named VCA, forklift, or food-safety certificate is valid before referral, after they learn which Studytube records count.

tasks.human_edge: The admin has to judge a messy CV, such as forklift experience without the certificate the site requires, and has to refuse a knockout that would screen people out unfairly. Referral of a person stays a human selection.
tasks.pattern_why: The checklist is a fixed pass over a written knockout list, but the referral is a selection decision on a person. The admin stays the lead, which this use requires.

in_practice.trigger: A new application arrives on a live Recruitee vacancy that has a knockout list.
steps: Store the vacancy knockouts on the job: licence class, VCA, forklift or food-safety certificate, site, shift, and right to work.
Read the application once into a pass, fail, or unclear mark per knockout, with the CV line cited.
The admin reviews every unclear mark and every name they might refer, and corrects wrong reads.
The admin refers the chosen names to the recruiter or hiring manager in Recruitee.
Clear fails stay in stage with the failed item visible, for the recruiter's rejection decision.
Once a week the admin and recruiter fix knockouts that no longer match the job.
in_practice.human_gate: The admin decides who is referred. The checklist never rejects or advances a candidate on its own.
data_needed: Approved knockout list per vacancy
Application and CV text
Certificate names and expiry the candidate has already provided
Site, shift, and contract type
Right-to-work status already held in the process
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee candidate notes, visible to the recruiter, with the checklist stored on the application and no second score kept outside Recruitee.

evidence.claim: A decision with legal effect on a person, including rejection, may not rest solely on automated processing. The letter can be automated; the selection cannot.
From 2 December 2027, AI used to screen applicants is a high-risk system under Annex III 4(a).
AI summaries of candidates become a paper trail. If the employer cannot say where that data goes, the tool is not ready.
Forklift, VCA, licence class, site, and shift can be written as knockouts. Whether a messy logistics CV meets them is still a judgment.

risks: Treating the checklist as the selection makes this a high-risk screening system from 2 December 2027.
A knockout such as 'native Dutch only' or a proxy for age can exclude people unlawfully, and a fluent checklist makes that look official.
The works council must consent if the tool processes candidate data in a new way or logs behaviour against people (WOR art. 27).
A stored summary can become the file the manager relies on, including a misread certificate.
research_questions: What share of warehouse applications fail on a written knockout, and what share turn on a judgment the checklist would mark unclear?
How often is a pass or fail wrong when someone checks it against the original CV?
Do hiring managers change who they interview when they see a strict list, an experience-equivalent list, and an internal-first list?
Will the works council treat this checklist as applicant screening that needs consent and, from December 2027, a high-risk AI file?

tasks.short: Tell applicants they are accepted or rejected.

today.trigger: A recruiter or hiring manager decides, then asks the admin to tell the applicant.
steps: Watch Recruitee or the recruiter's mail for the outcome.
Pick a template: reject after screening, reject after interview, offer, or welcome.
Merge name, role, site, start date, and the CAO scale the manager already approved.
Send it from Recruitee or Outlook and file a copy.
Answer replies, and for an acceptance start the onboarding checklist toward AFAS.
drudgery: Copying the same rejection into outgoing mail
Checking that the start date and site match the offer
Remembering which internal applicant must hear it from their manager first
Filing the sent mail on the candidate
today.time_sinks: Sensitive replies and internal applicants sit in the inbox while routine rejections wait behind them. Peak weeks multiply the same letter.

lenses.faster: Typing and sending the standard external rejection disappears once the recruiter sets the stage. Acceptance notes, internal applicants, and anyone who asks why still take a human pass. About 55% of the task time goes, mostly the bulk rejections.
lenses.autonomous: The recruiter's stage change in Recruitee starts it. Approved external rejection templates send without the admin. The admin releases every acceptance, every internal letter, and every request for reasons.
lenses.ambitious: Candidates refused for one missing certificate (VCA, forklift, or food safety) get that gap and the matching Studytube course in the letter, a service they do not get today, shared with the Learning and Development Specialist. Demand would grow if this were cheap: seasonal waves create many near-misses, and a clear no brings some of them back ready to hire.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss assembling rejection mail. The work they want is the acceptance handoff, so the dossier is complete before day one.
lenses.options: A bare no, a reason code with a reapply date, or a reason plus the missing course changes who comes back qualified. That changes the next shortlist, not only the time to send.
lenses.altitude: The week is no longer the Recruitee outbox. They keep the template set, pull a bad template, and handle the people who write back. They do not gain the right to accept or reject. The job becomes more expert on what a rejection may say, and less of a mail clerk.
reach: Recruiter: sending the standard stage letter and the approved offer pack, after they learn which CAO sentence Compensation and Benefits must sign.
Payroll Specialist: the new-hire signal that starts the person in the next pay cycle, after they learn which AFAS contract fields have to be present first.

tasks.human_edge: An internal colleague, and any candidate who asks why, needs the reason the panel actually gave, in words that do not invent a ground. The admin also catches a template that would tell the wrong person they are hired.
tasks.pattern_why: The outcome already exists as a Recruitee stage. A fixed template and merge fields send the message. A model writing fresh reasons would add wording the panel did not decide.

in_practice.trigger: A recruiter sets the candidate to rejected or hired in Recruitee.
steps: Match stage and candidate type to an approved template: external reject, internal reject, acceptance, welcome.
Merge name, role, site, start date, and contract type from Recruitee.
Send standard external rejections on that template and log them on the candidate.
Hold acceptances, internal applicants, and any conditional offer for the admin.
Route a reply that asks for reasons, or any upset reply, to the admin. The template does not continue the conversation.
On acceptance, open the existing onboarding checklist so AFAS and Studytube start from the same facts.
in_practice.human_gate: Standard external rejections send on the approved template. The admin releases every acceptance, every letter to an internal applicant, and every answer that gives a reason.
data_needed: Recruitee stage and who set it
Candidate type: external or internal
Template id approved by HR
Role, site, start date, contract type
The panel's reason code, where the template includes one
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee message history and the shared HR mailbox sent items, with the template id stored on the candidate.

evidence.claim: The acceptance or rejection letter may be produced automatically. The decision itself may not rest solely on automated processing.
Before launch, an HR bot joked about sick leave. Tone had to be fixed in configuration and in the instructions per topic.
SixFifty sends employer notices inside strict workflows on an expert-maintained rule base. That product's law base is US only.

Since 2 August 2026, people must be told they are interacting with an AI system unless that is already obvious. A fixed letter from the company is not such a conversation; a bot that answers the reply would be.

risks: A generated reason the panel never gave, or a reason that names health, age, or pregnancy, is an equal-treatment incident.
The wrong template can reject someone who was hired, or state the wrong site and start date.
Internal staff can receive the mail before their manager has spoken to them.
A chatbot that keeps answering replies needs an AI disclosure and can repeat the tone failure already seen on sick-leave topics.
research_questions: What share of outcomes are standard external rejections, and what share are internal applicants, offers, or people who ask for a reason?
How many rejection replies does HR get in a month, and how many of those can a template answer truthfully?
Does a missing-certificate line plus a Studytube course increase qualified reapplications without raising complaints?
Does the works council require a say on wording that goes to employees who applied internally?

tasks.short: Help employees with pension, allowances, and injury-pay paperwork.

today.trigger: An employee, manager, or the Compensation and Benefits Specialist asks about an allowance, pension, travel costs, or pay during illness or after an injury.
steps: Read the question in Outlook or Teams and identify the person in AFAS.
Look up contract, CAO, site, and shift pattern, then search the handbook or a prior mail.
Answer, or escalate when the CAO text does not settle it.
Collect enrolment and change forms and file them on the dossier.
For a work injury or long absence, pass the pay question to Payroll and keep medical detail in the absence file.
drudgery: Re-reading the CAO PDF for the same travel-cost or shift-allowance question
Explaining again that a flex worker is not in the company pension
Retyping form answers into AFAS
Hunting an old mail to see what was promised last time
today.time_sinks: Night-shift staff write during the shift and wait until morning. The same allowance question arrives from all three sites in slightly different words.

lenses.faster: Standard questions on shift allowance, travel costs, and which pension scheme applies are answered from AFAS and a maintained table, so the CAO PDF stays closed. Enrolments, exceptions, and every injury or sickness file still take their current time. About 35% of the task goes.
lenses.autonomous: An employee question opens a quoted answer with the clause and the AFAS fields beside it. The admin sends it and does the paperwork. Anything about a named person's health or injury never enters the quote.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift warehouse staff at all three sites, who today wait until the office opens, get a quoted answer on CAO allowances and travel costs during their shift. Demand would grow if this were cheap: people would ask before a payroll error, and correction volume would rise for a while.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss looking up the same travel-cost answer. The work they want is the difficult case beside Compensation and Benefits, such as a top-up dispute or a flex-to-perm transfer.
lenses.options: A quote under the transport CAO, under the warehouse CAO, or a clear 'you are paid by the agency' changes whether someone accepts a transfer or a permanent offer. That is a different decision, not a shorter mail.
lenses.altitude: Standard entitlement questions close without a wait for Compensation and Benefits. Cases that interpret the CAO, touch health, or involve garnishment still go upstairs. The job becomes more expert on the edge of the table, and less of a search through old mails.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: first-line allowance, travel, and pension-scheme questions, after they learn which articles are settled and which are an interpretation.
Payroll Specialist: checking that a quoted allowance matches the wage component used in the pay run, after they learn those component codes.

tasks.human_edge: The admin has to see when the person's contract, site, and CAO do not match the table, and has to keep sickness and injury details out of any prompt. A disappointing answer to someone on the floor still needs a person.
tasks.pattern_why: Entitlements are a lookup on contract, CAO, site, and shift. A model writing the figure would invent money. The admin still does enrolments and every case the table does not cover.

in_practice.trigger: An employee or manager asks about an allowance, pension, travel costs, or pay during illness.
steps: Identify the person in AFAS: contract type, CAO, site, shift, and whether they are agency staff.
Quote the matching row from the allowance and pension table, with the clause id beside the figure.
If the person is a flex worker, return the standing answer that the agency holds the employment, and name the agency contact route.
The admin checks the quote against AFAS and sends it, or escalates when the table has no row.
Enrolment and change forms stay with the admin and are filed on the dossier.
Questions about a person's health, injury, or Wet verbetering poortwachter file stay in the absence process and are not pasted into a prompt.
in_practice.human_gate: The admin sends every answer and handles every enrolment. The lookup does not write to payroll and does not touch the absence file.
data_needed: Contract type, CAO, site, and shift pattern
Allowance and pension table with clause ids, maintained by Compensation and Benefits
Agency-versus-employee flag
Wage-component codes Payroll has confirmed
No diagnosis, no recovery notes, no doctor's letter
in_practice.logs_to: The HR mailbox and the AFAS dossier note: clause id, fields used, and who sent the answer. Health details are not written into that note.

evidence.claim: SAP Joule's HR agents answer employee questions or dispatch them, and can explain a payslip. No customer result is published.
Coca-Cola Andina's HR agent answers differently by region, contract type, and tenure, from data synced daily. Unresolved questions become a ticket in the existing queue.
Danish chatbot users, including HR staff and clerks, saved about 3% of hours, and about 7% where employers pushed use. Hours came from redesigned work, not from a bot left beside the old process.
Sickness reporting under Wet verbetering poortwachter is rule-bound, but health data is special-category data and should stay out of model prompts.

risks: A wrong allowance quote that the employee relies on creates a payroll correction and a trust problem.
Pasting an injury or sickness mail into a prompt puts special-category data into a model log.
Flex workers can be answered as if they were in the company pension.
A bot that reads the personnel file to personalise an answer needs works-council consent under WOR art. 27(1)(k), and an AI disclosure under Art. 50 if people are talking to it.
Emotion inference on a frustrated caller is banned at work.
research_questions: What share of these contacts are standard allowance, travel, or pension questions, and what share are enrolments, injuries, or exceptions?
Are shift allowance and travel amounts fully fixed by CAO, site, and contract in AFAS, or does each one need interpretation?
Do night-shift staff currently wait, and does that wait show up as payroll corrections?
Will the works council allow a lookup that reads contract type and site from AFAS, and where must the answer say it came from software?

tasks.short: Post open jobs and tell eligible staff a role is available.

today.trigger: A recruiter approves a vacancy and asks the admin to publish it.
steps: Take the approved text and adapt it for the internal board, external boards, and a short Teams post.
Post it in Recruitee and on the channels the company uses.
Check the CAO internal-first period before any external post.
Search AFAS for staff who match function group, certificate, and site, then mail them.
Take the post down on the end date and tell the agencies if they are allowed to supply people.
drudgery: Pasting the same vacancy into several places
Rebuilding the eligible-staff list from AFAS
Remembering which CAO requires an internal window
Chasing a site manager for a posting that should have gone out yesterday
today.time_sinks: Night-shift and weekend staff never see the internal mail in time, so the internal window expires and the role goes external by default.

lenses.faster: Rewriting the approved vacancy for each channel, and rebuilding the eligible-staff list by hand, disappears. The admin still checks the text and the list before anything is sent. About 45% of the task time goes.
lenses.autonomous: An approved vacancy starts three drafts and a proposed recipient list. Nothing is posted and nobody is mailed until the admin approves that vacancy.
lenses.ambitious: Eligible floor staff on the night shift at Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo get the internal notice the same day, inside the CAO window, a group the morning mail currently misses. Demand would grow if this were cheap: short seasonal roles would use the internal window too, because the cost of a careful notice would drop.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss pasting vacancies into portals. The work they want is deciding who on the floor is actually ready for the role.
lenses.options: Internal only for the CAO window, internal plus job boards, or boards plus the three agencies changes who applies and what the agency fee is. A strict certificate list versus a broader one changes who is nudged. Both change the hire, not only the effort.
lenses.altitude: They run the posting calendar and can hold a post that skips the internal window or states pay outside the approved band. Channel choice stays with the recruiter when a role is hard to fill. The job becomes more expert on the CAO posting rules, and less on portal screens.
reach: Recruiter: routine posting, refresh, and takedown of live ads, after they learn the channel contracts and the internal-first period in both CAOs.
HR Business Partner: telling a site's eligible staff once the central vacancy is approved, after they learn which local custom the site manager may add.

tasks.human_edge: The admin has to judge the grey names: mid-certificate, on a performance plan, or someone a manager wants quietly left out. They also catch an ad that promises hours or pay the vacancy form does not, or that states a discriminatory requirement.
tasks.pattern_why: One pass turns the approved vacancy into the internal notice, the external post, and the staff mail. The channel rules and the internal-first wait are fixed. The steps do not need an agent deciding where to post.

in_practice.trigger: A recruiter marks a vacancy approved and ready to publish.
steps: Draft the internal notice, the external post, and the short Teams text from the approved vacancy.
Apply the internal-first wait from the relevant CAO before any external channel is offered.
Build the eligible list from AFAS on function group, site, and the certificates the vacancy names.
The admin edits the text, removes names, and approves the list.
On approval, publish to the chosen channels and mail the approved internal list.
Close the post on its end date and record whether agencies were allowed to supply.
in_practice.human_gate: The admin approves the text, the channel mix, and the recipient list for every vacancy before publication or mail.
data_needed: Approved vacancy text and salary band
Internal-first days per CAO
Channel list and which roles may go to agencies
Eligibility rules: function group, site, certificates
Employee work-email and shift pattern for timing the notice
in_practice.logs_to: The Recruitee job record and a SharePoint posting log: channels, dates, approver, and the eligibility rule used. Not a ranking of employees.

evidence.claim: Works-council consent is required for a system that processes personnel data (WOR art. 27(1)(k)). Choosing who is notified from the personnel file is that kind of processing.
From 2 December 2027, AI that screens applicants is high-risk. A policy question bot is not. An eligibility ranking sits near the screening line.
Publishing an already approved text to a known channel list is a routing rule. No source in the digest shows a product doing Dutch CAO vacancy posting.

risks: Mailing an 'you are eligible' list can become a selection decision and a works-council issue.
Skipping the internal-first window breaches the CAO.
An ad can pick up an unlawful requirement from an old vacancy text.
Agency portals can be notified late, so the company pays for candidates it could have filled internally.
Employees' certificate and shift data are personal data; the list needs a written rule and a retention period.
research_questions: For each CAO, which vacancies must be offered internally first, and for how many days?
How many internal names does a typical warehouse vacancy match, and how often do managers dispute the list?
Does a same-day notice to night shift raise internal applications without missing the seasonal start date?
Which boards can Recruitee already publish to, and where does someone still paste by hand?

tasks.short: Find file details and prepare an employer statement for an authorised requester.

today.trigger: A lender, debt administrator, bailiff, or employee asks for an employer statement or a file extract.
steps: Read the request and see who is asking, about whom, and for which fields.
Check for employee consent or a legal order such as loonbeslag.
Look up contract, hours, and salary components in AFAS.
Type them into the requester's form and have a colleague glance at it when unsure.
Send it and keep a copy. Refuse requests for sickness or injury detail.
drudgery: Retyping salary and hours into a different PDF for each lender
Hunting the right wage components
Matching a nickname or old surname to the right dossier
Filing the consent back onto the person
today.time_sinks: Shift staff cannot call during the day, so mortgage statements wait, and the lender chases HR by mail all week.

lenses.faster: Searching AFAS and retyping contract, hours, and salary into the form disappears. Every outgoing statement is still checked, and beslag or a missing consent stays slow. About 50% of the task time goes.
lenses.autonomous: An incoming request starts extraction of requester, employee, fields, and whether consent or an order is attached, then a fill from AFAS. Nothing is sent until the admin approves that statement.
lenses.ambitious: Employees on shifts, who today wait days for a mortgage or rental statement, request their own werkgeversverklaring and the admin releases a same-day statement to the lender they named. Demand would grow if this were cheap: more lenders and landlords would ask, so the service has to stay employee-initiated.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss typing figures into PDF forms. The work they want is the odd request: a bailiff, a bewindvoerder, a foreign lender, an ex-employee.
lenses.options: On a fixed-term contract, stating the end date alone, or the end date plus a true sentence that there is no current plan to end early, changes the lender's decision. Only sentences that are true are offered. The choice changes the mortgage, not the typing time.
lenses.altitude: The queue becomes requests with no basis, orders, health questions, and people who are not in AFAS. They can refuse a request that lacks consent or a legal order, using a written release matrix, without asking an HR Business Partner each time. The job becomes more expert on AVG release rules, and less on where a field sits in AFAS.
reach: Payroll Specialist: completing vast loon and hours on a standard werkgeversverklaring, after they learn which wage components lenders count.
Credit and Collections Officer: recognising a loonbeslag and routing it to payroll, after they learn the difference between a garnishment and a commercial credit enquiry.

tasks.human_edge: The admin has to decide whether this requester may receive these fields, refuse health and absence data, and keep the fixed-term sentence true. Sending the file is a disclosure the model must not make.
tasks.pattern_why: The request arrives as a messy mail or PDF. One pass turns it into requester, employee, fields, and basis, and AFAS fills the form. The release rules are fixed, so an agent browsing the dossier is unnecessary.

in_practice.trigger: A statement request arrives by mail, or an employee starts one from a form.
steps: Read the request into requester, employee, fields asked, and attachment type: consent, lender form, or court or bailiff order.
Reject the extract when there is no consent and no order, and when the fields include health or absence.
Fill the allowed fields from AFAS: contract, start date, hours, and the wage components the form is permitted to show.
Show the draft, the basis, and the source fields to the admin.
The admin approves, edits the fixed-term sentence, or refuses.
Store what was sent, to whom, and why, on the dossier, and give the employee a copy when the request was their own.
in_practice.human_gate: The admin approves every statement before it leaves the company. Missing consent, a garnishment, health data, and anyone not on the AFAS employee file always stop.
data_needed: The request document and its attachment
Employee identifier the admin confirms
Contract, hours, and permitted wage components
A release matrix: which fields go out on consent, and which on a court or bailiff order
No BSN in a prompt log unless the approved form requires it and the basis is recorded
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS dossier: requester, fields released, basis (consent or order), approver, and date. The document image stays in the dossier, not in a separate chat log.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8's Jonas reads documents into dossier fields. The published description gives no error rate.
Works-council consent applies when a system processes personnel-file data. A new reader over dossiers for outside disclosure is that kind of system.
Salary, BSN, and contract data may go to a lender or a bailiff only with employee consent or a legal obligation. A credit enquiry alone is not enough.
If an employer cannot say where data from an automated summary goes, the tool is not ready to use. Incoming requests can contain health details.

risks: Sending salary or a BSN to a requester with no consent and no order is a data breach.
A model log can keep a BSN or a diagnosis that was sitting in the incoming mail.
A soft sentence on a fixed-term contract can mislead a lender if it is not true.
Flex workers are often absent from the employee file; pulling them from an agency portal is a different basis.
The employee may never see what was said about them.
research_questions: How many employer statements and similar requests arrive per month, and what share lack consent or come from a bailiff?
Which wage components do the usual Dutch lender forms ask for, and are they all in AFAS without Payroll opening the file?
What is the current turnaround for shift staff, and how many chasing mails does a delayed statement produce?
Does Jonas read the form inside AFAS, who the subprocessors are, and what its error rate is on these forms?

tasks.short: Compile the personnel reports managers and the works council ask for.

today.trigger: The monthly HR meeting, a works-council request, or a manager asks for starters, leavers, headcount, absence, or contract ends.
steps: Pull figures from the Power BI dashboards and, where a cut is missing, from the AFAS extract into Excel.
Reconcile site, flex, and contract-type counts with last month's sheet.
Build the pack and add a short written note.
Send it to HR, Finance, or the works council.
Correct it after someone finds a double count.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same workbook each month
Splitting flex workers out of headcount by hand
Copying certificate dates from Studytube for a one-off mail
Explaining again why this month's headcount does not match Finance
today.time_sinks: The argument about whose number is right consumes the meeting. Small sites make a verzuim percentage point at one person, and someone has to notice before it is sent.

lenses.faster: Rebuilding the monthly Excel for starters, leavers, contract ends, headcount, and certificate expiry disappears. Those packs refresh from the nightly extract on fixed definitions. One-off questions and anomaly checks remain. About 70% of the task time goes.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS refresh starts the standard packs. They are published to the agreed audience on the calendar. The admin handles a new cut, a broken refresh, and any cell small enough to identify a person.
lenses.ambitious: Warehouse supervisors and the works council receive a weekly certificate-expiry pack by site and shift (forklift, VCA, food safety), in time to book Studytube before someone is stopped at the dock. They do not get this today. Demand would grow if it were cheap: every site would take a weekly list, because an expired certificate stops work.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the workbook. The work they want is explaining a figure that cannot be right, such as a flex worker counted twice.
lenses.options: Headcount with flex included, flex shown apart, and flex omitted change whether the works council and the Finance Director think the sites are over staffed. That choice changes hiring and agency orders, not only the chart.
lenses.altitude: Monday is a check of anomalies and suppressed cells, not a pivot-table afternoon. They can refuse a cut that would name someone's absence, and they share definition ownership with the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst. The job becomes more expert on definitions and privacy, and less on Excel.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: distributing the fixed monthly pack and watching the refresh, after they learn the extract's definitions and the small-cell rule.
Controller: the headcount bridge Finance uses at month close, after they learn Finance's flex rule and keep one definition.

tasks.human_edge: The admin can see a figure that will mislead the works council, such as double-counted flex or a Venlo cell that names one person's absence. The machine will publish whatever the definition says.
tasks.pattern_why: The packs are counts on agreed definitions from the nightly extract. A model writing a story about why absence moved would invent causes and can slide into performance or health monitoring.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract refreshes, and the calendar reaches a pack's send date.
steps: Refresh the fixed packs: headcount by site and contract, starters, leavers, contract ends, and certificate expiry.
Apply the flex rule agreed with Finance, and suppress any cell under the agreed size.
Publish verzuim only as a site rate above that size threshold, with no names.
The admin reviews anomalies and the suppressed cells, then releases the pack.
A manager who wants a new cut asks the admin, who builds it once and either adds it to the definitions or refuses it.
Archive the pack with the definition version on SharePoint.
in_practice.human_gate: Standard packs go out after the admin's anomaly check. Any new definition, any named absence, and any cell that identifies a person waits for the admin and, where it concerns the works council, the existing information route.
data_needed: Nightly AFAS extract and its field definitions
The flex counting rule agreed with Finance
Studytube certificate type and expiry
Minimum cell size for sharing
Distribution list per pack
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint report archive and the Power BI workspace, with the definition version and the name of the person who released the pack.

evidence.claim: From 2 December 2027, AI that monitors performance or allocates tasks is high-risk. A pack of agreed counts is not that use. A narrative that judges people would be close to it.
Chatbot users saved about 3% of hours. The measured lesson is that hours move when the old workflow is replaced, not when a helper sits beside it.
Emotion inference at work is prohibited. A written cause such as 'this site is disengaged' is the kind of inference to avoid in a personnel pack.
Standard headcount and movement reports can be produced from a nightly HR extract with fixed definitions. The company already refreshes Power BI from AFAS each night.

risks: A verzuim or performance cut on a small Venlo or night-shift team identifies a person.
Flex counted twice makes the works council and Finance argue from different headcounts.
Commentary that invents a cause for absence processes health data and can become performance monitoring.
Certificate data shared too widely shows who is not allowed to operate equipment, which is personal data.
If Excel stays in use beside the pack, the hours do not move.
research_questions: Which packs are still Excel, and which are already a Power BI page someone could share?
How often is a published HR number corrected after the meeting, and what caused the correction?
What cell size still identifies a person at each site and shift?
Is Studytube certificate expiry in the nightly extract, and would warehouse managers act on a weekly list?

tasks.short: Update the handbook, org chart, directory, and evaluation forms.

today.trigger: Someone joins, leaves, or moves, or HR changes a policy, a form, or the handbook.
steps: Update the org chart and the SharePoint directory from what a manager reports.
Find the current handbook or form and edit a copy in Word.
Ask the HR Business Partner or Compensation and Benefits whether the sentence is right.
Route real regulation changes through the works council.
Publish the file and tell the sites, then discover an old PDF is still circulating.
drudgery: Dragging boxes on the org chart after every transfer
Hunting the live handbook among copies
Retyping a directory page that AFAS already knows
Checking three sites' folders for an old evaluation form
today.time_sinks: A one-line policy change waits on finding the right file and the right owner. Meanwhile supervisors use a PDF saved on a shift PC.

lenses.faster: Rebuilding the org chart and the directory after each move disappears; they follow AFAS. A handbook or form change arrives as a redline against the live SharePoint file. The admin still checks meaning and still walks regulation changes through the works council. About 60% of the task time goes.
lenses.autonomous: An AFAS change to team, manager, or site updates the directory and the org chart. A decided policy change starts a redline of the handbook or the blank form. Publication of any wording waits for the admin.
lenses.ambitious: Flex workers and night-shift supervisors, who today hear rules second-hand, get a one-page sheet of the rules that apply to their contract and site, updated with the handbook. Demand would grow if this were cheap: every policy change would be pushed to the floor, and each agency would ask for a flex sheet at the start of the season.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss maintaining the chart or chasing old PDFs. The work they want is the wording check with the HR Business Partner, so the floor version matches what the works council agreed.
lenses.options: A full article and a plain-Dutch floor version of the same change, and an org chart that shows flex leads or hides them, change which rule a supervisor applies and what span of control looks like. The plain version has to keep the same meaning or the decision is accidental.
lenses.altitude: The week is AFAS exceptions (empty site, wrong manager) and redlines waiting on an owner or the works council. They can block a quiet edit that changes a regulation without the consent route. The job becomes more expert on which documents are regulations, and less of a desktop-publishing job.
reach: HR Business Partner: drafting the site instruction that follows a central handbook change, after they learn local custom at each site versus the CAO.
Learning and Development Specialist: keeping the certificate page of the handbook aligned with the mandatory courses, after they learn which certificates are statutory and which are company rules.

tasks.human_edge: The admin has to know which sentence is a regulation that needs the works council, and whether a plainer sentence changed the meaning. They also keep the evaluation form as a blank form, not a scorer of people.
tasks.pattern_why: Directory and org chart follow AFAS with no model. A handbook or form change is one redline against a known file. The route is predictable, so an agent should not edit the live handbook.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS records a change of team, manager, or site, or an owner submits a decided handbook or form change.
steps: Update the directory and org chart from AFAS org units, manager, site, and work phone.
When a wording change is submitted, produce a redline against the live SharePoint file and name the CAO or policy clause.
Mark whether the change is a contact detail, a company rule, or a regulation that needs the works council.
The chapter owner (HR Business Partner, Compensation and Benefits, Learning and Development, or Payroll) confirms the meaning.
The admin publishes only after that confirmation, and after works-council consent where WOR requires it.
Withdraw the old PDF from the site folders and post the flex and night-shift sheet when the change affects them.
in_practice.human_gate: The admin approves every publication of wording. Org chart and directory rows that AFAS can fill update on their own, and any row with a missing manager or a private number stops for the admin.
data_needed: AFAS org unit, manager, site, and published phone
The live handbook and forms on SharePoint
The decided change and its clause
Chapter owner per section
Works-council status for regulation changes
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history, with the works-council file number when a regulation changed, and the owner who confirmed the redline.

evidence.claim: SixFifty drafts handbooks and contracts and sends them for signature inside strict workflows on an attorney-built law base. The base is US law, so the pattern is the workflow, not the clauses.
AFAS Profit 8 reads documents into dossier fields and holds the employee record the org chart has to follow. No error rate is published.
At Coca-Cola Andina, content structure mattered more than the model. A named HR owner per region writes the knowledge the assistant may use.
Works-council consent is required before introducing or changing a personnel regulation or a system that processes personnel data (WOR art. 27).

risks: A plain-language edit can change a CAO right or a regulation without anyone noticing.
Publishing before works-council consent breaches WOR art. 27.
An org chart can reveal pregnancy cover, sickness cover, or a private mobile number.
'Help' with performance forms can drift into scoring people, which is high-risk monitoring from 2 December 2027, and emotion inference is already banned.
A US handbook workflow will not know the two Dutch CAOs or the works council.
Old PDFs on shift PCs keep circulating if takedown is not part of the change.
research_questions: How many handbook changes a year need works-council consent, and how many are only names, phones, or org boxes?
Is the AFAS org structure complete enough that a chart needs no manual boxes?
Do night-shift supervisors use the SharePoint handbook today, or a saved PDF?
Who is the named owner of each chapter: HR Business Partner, Compensation and Benefits, Learning and Development, or Payroll?

role.altitude: The two administrators stop being the people who retype dossiers, letters, and workbooks. Their week becomes the exception queues: unclear applicants, sensitive letters, entitlement cases the table cannot price, data requests without a basis, report cells that would name a person, and handbook lines that need the works council. They gain the right to refuse an unfounded file release, hold a vacancy that skips the internal window, send back a knockout list that is incomplete, and block a handbook edit that changes a regulation. They do not gain hire, pay, or dismissal decisions. The job becomes more expert on AVG, the two CAOs, and WOR, and less clerical.
reach: Recruiter: pipeline cleanup, standard posting, and stage letters, after they learn Recruitee stages and the certificate knockouts.
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: first-line allowance and pension questions, after they learn which CAO articles are settled.
Payroll Specialist: wage components on a standard employer statement, after they learn what counts as vast loon.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: release of the fixed monthly pack, after they learn definitions and small-cell suppression.
Learning and Development Specialist: the handbook's certificate page and pre-referral certificate checks, after they learn which certificates are statutory.
HR Business Partner: the site instruction that follows a central handbook change, after they learn local custom at Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo.
role.ceiling_note: These seven tasks are 26.5% of the role on the hours supplied. Each design leaves a review, a works-council step, or an exception, and peak season adds 150 to 300 flex workers whose chasing is coordination. Health data, applicant selection, and anything sent outside the company stay with a person. The ceiling is two administrators closing exceptions for three sites and all shifts. It is not a smaller HR team, and the other three-quarters of the role is outside this list.
skills_to_grow: AVG bases for releasing employee data: consent, loonbeslag, and what a commercial enquiry may not have
Internal-first, allowance, and sickness-pay articles of both CAOs, at policy level, without reading medical files
WOR art. 27: which document changes and which tools need works-council consent
Recruitee stages, AFAS dossier fields, and what Jonas is allowed to read
Power BI definition ownership and small-cell suppression for the works council
EU AI Act boundaries: applicant screening and performance monitoring from 2 December 2027, and AI disclosure when staff talk to a bot
Writing knockout lists and entitlement tables so software can quote them without inventing a sentence
role.ambitious_version: The desk answers all three sites on the same day, including the night shift. Overnight warehouse applications are checked against the vacancy before the shift lead arrives. Eligible floor staff hear about an internal vacancy inside the CAO window. A shift worker can get a quoted allowance answer, and a same-day employer statement, without calling Rotterdam in the morning. Supervisors see certificate expiry in time to book the course. Flex workers get a short sheet of what applies to them and what stays with the agency. The administrators keep those tables and wording current with the works council, and the recruiters, HR Business Partners, and Compensation and Benefits see the exceptions and the day-90 result.
